name: zzCH3_regress_colours

tests.name: the mascot style settings can be read back

detail.note: a setting that cannot be read cannot be restored, and this job changes a colourway the founder may have chosen.

tests.name: the wardrobe is open through the founder's own button
the preview window reports where it is
the console commands set the colourway the founder typed

detail.note: read back from the settings object rather than trusting the command. The founder's route is the console; the settings object is the record.

tests.name: the colourway the job found was put back

detail.note: a job that leaves a colourway changed makes every later capture in this session -- and every other lane's -- a photograph of this job.

tests.name: every frame is a different picture

detail.note: if setting a colourway changed nothing on screen the frames are identical and every fraction below would be the same number twice. Counts ALL frames rather than a hard-coded two: this clause went red the moment a third frame was added, on a run where all three were distinct, which is a bookkeeping failure wearing the costume of a real one.

the founder's PRIMARY is the main colourway, so it should cover a large part of the figure. Judged against the cleared frame, because finding green proves nothing unless the same figure without a colourway has none.

tests.name: SECONDARY visibly changes the eye colour, and the body does not follow it

detail.note: ASKED AS 'DID THE EYES CHANGE', not 'is there magenta'. The channel multiplies, so a magenta SECONDARY on gold eyes renders PINK -- measured at RGB 0.929, 0.430, 0.483 against 0.485, 0.798, 0.467 for a cyan one, a move of 0.444. The old clause counted magenta pixels and found none through every run while the eyes were plainly changing, and its upper bound -- SECONDARY must not reach the body -- passed just as happily when SECONDARY reached nothing at all.
